$$w^{2}+z^{2}-w z=w^{2}+z^{2}-\frac{(w+z)^{2}-\left(w^{2}+z^{2}\right)}{2}=\frac{3}{2}\left(w^{2}+z^{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}(w+z)^{2}.$$
Hence,
$$\left|w^{3}+z^{3}\right|=\left|\frac{3}{2}\left(w^{2}+z^{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}(w+z)^{2}\right|.$$
From the triangle inequality, we have
$$\left|\frac{3}{2}\left(w^{2}+z^{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}(w+z)^{2}\right| \geq\left|\frac{3}{2}\left|w^{2}+z^{2}\right|-\frac{1}{2}\left|(w+z)^{2}\right|\right|=\left|\frac{3}{2}(14)-\frac{1}{2}(1)\right|=\left|21-\frac{1}{2}\right|=\frac{41}{2}.$$
Also,
$$\left|\frac{3}{2}\left(w^{2}+z^{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}(w+z)^{2}\right| \leq \frac{3}{2}\left|w^{2}+z^{2}\right|+\frac{1}{2}|w+z|^{2}=\frac{3}{2}(14)+\frac{1}{2}(1)=21+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{43}{2}.$$
We want to find the smallest possible value of $\left|w^{3}+z^{3}\right|$.
